title: Tag Management Studio Cutover And Analytics Retirement Delivery
summary: Move the existing tag data, services, routes, editors, tests, and checks into Studio, then retire the remaining Analytics application without aliases or dual ownership.
content_html:
Tag Management Studio Cutover And Analytics Retirement Delivery

Status

This is an active delivery. TMS-P0 through TMS-P2 are complete. Studio now owns the canonical tag source, retained policy, domain services, transactions, activity integration, /studio/api/tags/... boundary, and all five retained browser workflows. TMS-P3 parity proof is next; Analytics has not yet been retired.

Detailed pre-cutover evidence is in the temporary TMS-P0 Freeze.

Outcome

Studio becomes the sole owner of canonical tags, aliases, assignments, group descriptions, tag policy, and their current maintenance workflows. The standalone Analytics application, server, routes, runner, tests, and check ownership are then removed.

This is a lift-and-shift ownership cutover, not a tag-model or UI redesign. Stable tag, Series, and Work identities and all current assignment relationships remain unchanged.

Completion unblocks implementation of Semantic Tokens, but no semantic-token registry, authoring, rendering, relationship, or report work is part of this delivery.

Benefits And Risks

Benefits:

  • canonical catalogue and tag data share one Studio owner and runtime;
  • Studio catalogue generation no longer imports an Analytics package;
  • one local app, API surface, port, runner, route shell, and check family can be retired;
  • later tag consumers, including Semantic Tokens, can read a stable Studio-owned source without preserving an application due for removal.

Main risks:

  • changing canonical IDs, normalization, assignment inheritance, or alias history during what should be an ownership move;
  • weakening preview/apply, multi-file atomicity, rollback, or activity evidence;
  • losing staged offline assignment sessions during the route move;
  • moving only the visible editors while leaving catalogue generation, Admin audits, tests, configuration, or runners coupled to analytics-app/;
  • carrying Analytics shell, Data Sharing, stale CSS, or compatibility routes into Studio unnecessarily.

Current Boundary

Studio owns:

  • the four unchanged canonical files under studio/data/canonical/tags/;
  • retained group-order, coverage, and RAG policy in studio/data/config/tags/tag-management.json;
  • the model, source paths, planners, transaction and rollback boundary, activity integration, and route constants under studio/services/tags/;
  • tag request/result adapters and dispatch under /studio/api/tags/...;
  • focused Python tests and fixtures, plus catalogue and Admin consumers of the Studio source-path package.

Studio also owns the five route templates, browser workflows, focused tag UI text and CSS, runtime configuration, and their positive API/browser smokes. Analytics temporarily retains only its standalone shell/home runtime pending TMS-P4; it has no tag routes, services, policy, retained workflow modules, or tag smoke profile.

The existing offline assignment session already uses dotlineform.studio.tagAssignmentsOffline.v1; preserve that storage key and the tag_assignments_offline_v1 payload contract so valid staged work survives the route move.

Target Ownership

Expected Studio owners:

studio/
├── data/
│   ├── canonical/tags/
│   │   ├── tag-registry.json
│   │   ├── tag-aliases.json
│   │   ├── tag-assignments.json
│   │   └── tag-groups.json
│   └── config/tags/
│       └── tag-management.json
│           group order, coverage policy, and other retained tag policy
├── services/tags/
│   model, path, planners, transactions, activity, and route constants
├── app/
│   ├── server/studio/
│   │   └── Studio tag API adapters and dispatch
│   └── frontend/
│       ├── routes/
│       └── js/
│           Studio-hosted tag workflows
└── tests/
    tag model, mutation, transaction, API, route, and browser contracts

The exact module split may follow existing Studio server conventions, but these roles must not remain under an Analytics namespace. Studio route paths use /studio/...; tag APIs use a Studio-owned /studio/api/tags/... boundary.

The public /analysis/ Docs Viewer scope is unaffected. Its name does not imply an Analytics application.

Preserved Contract

  • The four canonical JSON schemas and current records move without semantic transformation.
  • Canonical tag IDs remain <group>:<slug>.
  • Series-first assignments, nested Work override deltas, weights, alias context, and effective-tag derivation remain unchanged.
  • Registry and alias import, create, edit, delete, promote, and demote behavior remain available.
  • Destructive or cross-file changes retain preview before apply.
  • Multi-file writes retain validation, atomic replacement, rollback, and one initiating activity context.
  • Series coverage and the one-series editor retain their present meaning.
  • Direct writes, supported manual-patch fallback, and the versioned offline assignment session retain their current boundaries.

Presentation may be adapted only as required to fit the Studio shell, route, ready/busy, modal, transport, and styling conventions.

Not In Scope

  • redesigning tag schemas, groups, weights, scoring, assignments, aliases, or editor workflows;
  • adding Tag Dimensions, LLM-assisted tagging, Semantic Tokens, public tag pages, or new analysis features;
  • restoring tag-package or generic Data Sharing behavior;
  • retaining /analytics/... redirects, proxies, aliases, a shell stub, or a second canonical source;
  • moving the whole Analytics stylesheet or shell infrastructure when only attributed tag-route rules are live;
  • broad Studio visual polish unrelated to functional route integration.

Ordered Steps

[x] TMS-P0 — Freeze The Existing Contract

  • Record byte hashes and counts for all four canonical JSON files.
  • Map the five live routes, read/write endpoints, tag policy, activity actions, offline-session contract, current tests, and non-Analytics importers.
  • Attribute the frontend modules and CSS required by live tag routes; classify stale Analytics or Data Sharing remnants for retirement rather than transfer.
  • Confirm there is no remaining tag-package or document-package dependency.

Checkpoint: the exact behavior and active dependency boundary are known before any owner or path changes.

[x] TMS-P1 — Establish Studio Tag Data And Domain Ownership

  • Move the four canonical files into studio/data/canonical/tags/ without changing their bytes, records, IDs, or schemas.
  • Move retained tag policy from Analytics config into a focused Studio-owned config source.
  • Move the tag model, source paths, planners, transactions, activity integration, and route constants into studio/services/tags/.
  • Move the HTTP request/result adapters behind the Studio server's explicit tag API dispatch.
  • Retarget Studio catalogue generation/cleanup and Admin consistency checks to the Studio-owned source paths and modules.
  • Move focused Python tests and fixtures to Studio ownership.

Checkpoint: Studio owns and proves canonical reads, validation, plans, transactions, rollback, and API payloads; no canonical tag source remains in Analytics.

[x] TMS-P2 — Move The Tag Workflows Into The Studio App

  • Register Studio routes for Tag Groups, Tag Registry, Tag Aliases, Series Tags, and the Series Tag Editor.
  • Move the tag-specific templates, browser modules, UI text, and attributed CSS into Studio; use Studio shell, route registry, runtime config, transport, modal, ready/busy, theme, and public-link owners.
  • Point browser reads and writes at the Studio tag API.
  • Preserve current query identity, offline-session storage key and schema, preview/confirm behavior, and save-mode rules.
  • Update activity-contract route ownership while retaining current action and record meanings.
  • Move durable API and route/module smokes under Studio.

Checkpoint: every retained tag workflow runs through Local Studio without starting or calling Local Analytics.

[ ] TMS-P3 — Prove The Cutover

  • Recompare canonical bytes, counts, IDs, aliases, assignments, and group prose with the P0 freeze.
  • Prove read paths plus representative assignment, registry, alias, promote/demote, preview/no-write, apply, rollback, and activity contracts.
  • Prove Studio route boot and service integration at durable boundaries; leave ordinary visual and tactile review to manual Studio inspection.
  • Prove catalogue generation/cleanup and Admin consistency checks without an Analytics import path.
  • Verify public catalogue artifacts are unchanged unless a pre-existing regeneration difference is separately explained.

Checkpoint: Studio is the only runtime and source owner, with behavioral and data parity demonstrated before deletion.

[ ] TMS-P4 — Retire Analytics

  • Remove analytics-app/, bin/local-analytics, Analytics startup from bin/local-all, and Analytics messaging from bin/local-studio.
  • Remove Analytics host/port/runtime settings, route registry, server, shell, assets, tests, smoke profile, Admin route/check configuration, activity route references, and source-tree classifications.
  • Retarget only still-valid tag checks to Studio; remove tests that protect the retired shell or old paths rather than a retained capability.
  • Confirm no active code, config, runner, check, or browser module refers to /analytics/, analytics-app/, ANALYTICS_APP_*, or the old Python package.
  • Do not add redirects, proxies, compatibility imports, duplicate JSON, or an empty Analytics placeholder.

Checkpoint: the repository and local runners contain no Analytics application or runtime dependency.

[ ] TMS-P5 — Update Durable Owners And Close

  • Rewrite Tag Source Data, Tag Services, and the five tag workflow documents for their shipped Studio routes and owners.
  • Update Source Tree Ownership, Studio/Analytics overviews and roadmaps, local runtime guidance, configuration maps, and check documentation where their current contract changed.
  • Mark Tag Management In Studio and Analytics App Retirement complete only after all preceding gates pass.
  • Record Semantic Tokens as unblocked but leave its delivery proposed and untouched.
  • Run the mandatory end-of-delivery review for ownership drift, duplicate contracts, compatibility residue, dead Analytics paths, and overstated evidence.

Checkpoint: current documentation routes directly to Studio-owned code and data, and no active document instructs a user to run or maintain Analytics.

Completion Gates

  • [x] Studio is the sole canonical tag-data and tag-write owner.
  • [x] All five retained workflows are available through Local Studio.
  • [ ] Existing schema, identity, relationship, mutation, offline-session, and activity contracts are preserved.
  • [x] Studio catalogue and Admin checks have no Analytics import dependency.
  • [ ] analytics-app/, its runner, routes, APIs, configuration, checks, and runtime settings are removed without aliases.
  • [ ] The public /analysis/ Docs Viewer scope and current public catalogue outputs remain valid.
  • [ ] Focused Python, service/API, browser-module, runner/config, and cross-boundary checks pass at their actual scope.
  • [ ] Durable documentation describes the shipped Studio owner and retirement.
  • [ ] Semantic Tokens is unblocked but not implemented by this delivery.

Delivery State

Current state: active; TMS-P2 moved Tag Groups, Tag Registry, Tag Aliases, Series Tags, and Series Tag Editor into the Studio route shell. Their browser modules now use Studio config, transport, modal, ready/busy, theme, public-link, and activity owners. Query identity, the dotlineform.studio.tagAssignmentsOffline.v1 storage key, tag_assignments_offline_v1 payload version, preview/confirm flow, and save-mode rules remain unchanged. Analytics no longer registers or configures tag routes or services.

Focused Studio tag Python/API checks pass 64/64. The positive studio-tag-smoke profile passes 10/10 using one temporary Studio server; it proves all five routes, same-origin /studio/api/tags/... reads/writes, route readiness, query-driven Series Tag Editor loading, and module wiring without starting or calling Local Analytics. The quick profile passes 7/7. No test was added to assert the absence of the retired application.

Evidence:

  • var/admin/test-runs/tms-p2-studio-tag-cutover-rerun/summary.md;
  • var/admin/test-runs/tms-p2-quick-rerun/summary.md;
  • TMS-P0 Freeze for the byte and behavior baseline.

Next checkpoint: TMS-P3 re-runs the P0 parity comparisons and representative mutation, rollback, activity, catalogue, Admin, and public-output proofs. Do not start TMS-P3, Analytics retirement, or Semantic Tokens implementation without the next explicit approval.
